summary: Full regression on Node/Express backend rewrite plus new Absence History feature. 26/26 pytest tests passed (health, workspace lookup, auth guards incl. workspace_missing/wrong_workspace, team CRUD + role guards, employees CRUD with role-scoped salary redaction, absences CRUD with bad-date validation and cross-workspace 404, reports upload filename+magic-bytes validation and role-based access filtering). Frontend E2E on ?w=acme-steel: login as admin succeeds, Employees search triggers ?search= API call, history-employee-{id}-button opens absence-modal, add + delete round-trip works (verified via network trace to /api/employees/{id}/absences and /api/absences/{id}), Reports upload modal renders, Team & roles link visible for admin, and ?w=ghost-factory renders workspace-missing screen.
critical_code_review_comments: server.js:223 uses `.or(name.ilike.%${search}%,role.ilike.%${search}%)` without escaping — a search term containing commas or parentheses could break the PostgREST filter. Consider sanitizing/escaping the search string.
server.js:292 deletes absences via a separate query before deleting an employee. Wrapping this in a single Postgres RPC/transaction would prevent orphaned rows if the second delete fails.
server.js:385 checks only the first 4 magic bytes `%PDF`. That's fine, but combine with mimetype validation for defense in depth.
App.js is 840 lines with many modals inline — consider splitting AbsenceHistoryModal, EmployeeForm, ReportUploadModal, TeamModal into their own files for maintainability.
